gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Vortex Radar found the Botslab G980H 4-camera kit's front camera uses a 5 MP SmartSens SC501AI sensor recording 1620p at 25 fps, with the rear and both side cameras at 1080p at 25 fps and its 2160p mode called "fake 4K".
standout_why: Compared against milewitness.com and truepicked.com (both opened): neither names a 4-channel camera and neither carries a reviewer measurement, only maker specs and Reddit anecdotes. Our own page at rank 8 (dealectric.com/best-4-channel-dash-cam) already has the DashCamTalk F17 Plus bitrates (16/10/10/10 Mbps) and The Smart Home Hookup's 0.4 Wh parking figure for the Rexing R4-RD, so the only new items are Vortex Radar's sensor and frame-rate read on the G980H and DashCamTalk's F17 Plus scores. Tom's Guide's article body was truncated when fetched, so it was not compared. No named reviewer or lab has published a side-by-side measurement of 4-channel cameras under $200; the angle is thin.
decides: It confirms the pick more than it changes it. Of the under-$200 four-channel candidates, only two have any named-reviewer data: the Botslab G980H 4-camera (front, rear, left, right; our link) and the REDTIGER F17 Plus (front, front cabin, rear cabin, rear; $189.99 at redtigercam.com on 2026-11-21). I found no named-reviewer measurement for any of the cameras ChatGPT recommended (Rexing C4, LAMTTO DC21 and DC25, HUPEJOS V7). So the G980H is the honest row for a shopper who wants side views with some independent evidence, with its 25 fps and 5 MP front sensor stated plainly. The F17 Plus is the documented alternative for cabin views, at 30 fps with a Sony STARVIS 2 IMX675 front sensor.

findings.label: Front sensor and recording mode, identified by Vortex Radar
findings.value: 5 MP SmartSens SC501AI; front 1620p at 25 fps
findings.source_title: Botslab G980H Review (DashCamTalk forum, Vortex Radar, post #1, Apr 23, 2026)
findings.note: Vortex Radar describes the kit as "4CH setup: front, rear, left, right". The page text as fetched reads "Records at 1620p25 in 3CH mode"; re-check that wording against the post before printing, since the kit is 4-channel. My arithmetic: 2880 × 1620 = 4,665,600 pixels, which fits a 5 MP sensor. The review itself is an embedded video; only the post text was read.

findings.label: Rear and side cameras, per Vortex Radar
findings.source_title: Botslab G980H Review (DashCamTalk forum, Vortex Radar, post #1, Apr 23, 2026)
findings.note: Matches Botslab's own 25 fps figure in our product record. Vortex Radar gives no bitrate, codec or power draw in the post text.

findings.label: 4K mode, per Vortex Radar
findings.value: "Fake 4K mode at 2160p25 when running in 2-3 CH mode"
findings.source_title: Botslab G980H Review (DashCamTalk forum, Vortex Radar, post #1, Apr 23, 2026)
findings.note: My arithmetic: 3840 × 2160 = 8,294,400 pixels, more than a 5 MP sensor captures, so the 2160p mode is upscaled. It is not available with all four cameras attached. Vortex Radar also calls the G-sensor "really low sensitivity" (no figure).

findings.label: Cold-weather behaviour and data transfer, per Holger Becker (Smartzone)
findings.value: No cold-related failures on the 4-channel kit; the earlier 2-channel G980H stopped recording at around -15 °C; "langsame Datenübertragung" (slow data transfer) listed as a drawback
findings.source_title: Botslab Dashcam G980H 4-Kanal System Test: Überwacht ALLES (smartzone.de, Holger Becker, tested 16 Feb 2026)
findings.note: Observations, not instrumented measurements: no temperature is given for the 4-channel test and no transfer speed. The article also lists a hardwire-kit cut-off of 11.8 V ± 0.2 V, which looks like a maker spec. German unit, priced at 208 €.

findings.label: Per-channel resolution, frame rate and bitrate in DashCamTalk's database
findings.value: Front 2560 × 1440 at 30 fps, 16.0 Mbps (Sony STARVIS 2 IMX675); rear, interior and interior rear each 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps, 10.0 Mbps; H.264; capacitor
findings.source_title: REDTIGER F17 Plus (DashCamTalk dash cam database, updated November 21, 2026)
findings.note: The page does not say whether the bitrates were measured from files or taken from the maker. My arithmetic: 16 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 46 Mbps, which is 20.7 GB per hour and about 6.2 hours on the included 128 GB card (video only). The four views are front, front cabin, rear cabin and rear, not left and right. Our existing page already carries the bitrates.

findings.label: DashCamTalk scores
findings.value: Overall 6.7/10; day video 7/10; night video 6/10; reliability 6/10; value 9/10
findings.source_title: REDTIGER F17 Plus (DashCamTalk dash cam database, updated November 21, 2026)
findings.note: Editorial scores, not instrument readings. The page also lists parking mode as non-buffered plus timelapse, GPS yes, operating range -20 °C to 70 °C and microSD up to 512 GB.

findings.note: Neither figure is a measured speed. sm1ke used a unit supplied by Redtiger for about a week and says clips download as fast as on other dash cams. The 20 MB/s claim is from the redtigercam.com product listing read 2026-11-21.
